title: Isla, Rob and Mum: the clocks, a series and a scam
instr1: Isla lives in Edinburgh, and her brother Rob lives in Toronto. Every Sunday they have a video call about the series they're both watching. It's Saturday 24 October. In the UK, the clocks go back tonight; in Canada, a week later. Say each missing bit, then tap to check.
instr2: That evening, in the family group chat. Isla and Rob have just finished their series, so they need a new one. Say each missing bit, then tap to check.

part1.intro: WhatsApp · Isla and Rob · Saturday 24 October

p: Hi!

p.n: a heads-up — с a: просто предупреждаю

p: (heads-up): our clocks go back tonight, but yours don't change till next weekend.
So tomorrow's call will be

p.n: an hour later — так обычно говорят; one hour — когда важно число (один, а не два)

p: (one / an?) — 3 pm your time.

p.n: does + work — без -s: Does that still work?

p: (work / works?)
Thanks for the heads-up! Last year I sat in front of my laptop for an hour, wondering where you were 😂
But three's tricky —

p.n: время, которое назвал другой: at that time (или then), не ~~at this time~~

p: (this / that?).

p.n: Could (или Can) we make it + время? — так переносят встречу

p: (make) two, like always? That's six your time.
😂 I remember! Six works for me 👍
Well, the clocks went back, and Hamish still woke me up at his usual time. Which is five now 🙄
😂 Nobody told Hamish about

p.n: the clock change — существительное; а глагол: the clocks go back / change the clocks

p: (clock · change).
Seriously, it really

p.n: affect + что, без предлога: affects my sleep (но: an effect on)

p: (affect · I). I'll be a zombie all week.
Poor you. Changing the clocks does more harm than good, if you ask me.
Hamish clearly agrees 🐶
Sunday, 6:03 pm (Edinburgh)
Sorry! Running five minutes late — stuck in traffic 🙈
No worries! Hamish and I aren't going anywhere 😴
Mum, Rob and I need a new series for our Sunday calls. Any ideas?
YES!!! Too Good to Be True! It's about scams. My friend Moira

p.n: кому — с to, в конце: recommended it to me

p: (recommend · it · me), and I watched all eight episodes in one weekend 😎
Mum!! 😂 Were you up till two again?
Maybe 🙈 But everyone at my yoga class is talking about it!
Everyone at work

p.n: everyone keeps — с -s, как she keeps
going ON about — без on не говорят; keeps going on about it = уже надоели этим (or: won't stop talking about it)

p: (keep / keeps? + 1 small word) too.

p.n: any good — с be: Is it any good? (не ~~Does it any good?~~)

p: (Is / Does?), though? Isla, have you seen it?

p.n: I've only seen — have не пропадает

p: (I · see · bits). Mum had it on when I was at her place. The acting's brilliant, I'll give it that. But it looked a bit slow.
It's slow at first, but it really picks up in episode three.

p.n: worth — с be: it's worth it (не ~~it worth~~)

p: (It / It's?)
OK, OK,

p.n: решаю прямо сейчас → I'll: I'll give it a try

p: (I / I'll? · give) 😂
And you won't believe what happened on Friday! I got a text from “my bank”: your card has been blocked, click this link. Someone

p.n: pretend to be — выдавать себя за

p: (pretend) from the bank!
Oh no! You didn't click, did you??
Of course not. I've seen all eight episodes. Case closed 😎
Impressive, Mum! 👏
Nice one, Mum! By the way, I've got a new phone number. I'll text you from it now — save it!
Just got a message from an unknown number: “Hi Mum, it's me, new number.”

p.n: there's a scam going around — ходит такой развод

p: (scam) EXACTLY like this! Episode four! 🕵️‍♀️
Mum, that's Rob. He's just told you!
Mum, it's really me!
That's exactly what a scammer would say.
OK, ask me something only I would know. I'll answer from the new number.
Five minutes later
I asked “my son” what he broke when he was seven. Answer: “The kitchen window. With a football. Sorry again.”
Hmm. Fine. Number saved 😘

p.n: recommend + что: recommend the series (не ~~recommend me to watch~~)

p: (значит, не советуешь?), then, Rob?
Are you kidding? I'd definitely recommend it. Mum's now 100% scam-proof 😂
Wait till you get to episode four, you two 🕵️‍♀️
